findings.claim: For 5-mark questions, remember to include a specific Qur'an reference and explain how it connects to the belief.
findings.truth: The question that demands a source of wisdom and authority is worth 6 marks. The five-part question runs 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks and is worth 24 in total. Lessons 1 to 4 all label it a 6-mark question, so lesson 5 also contradicts its own unit.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments and 4.4.1 Component 1: 'marks will be allocated as follows: 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12'; each five-part question is worth 24 marks

findings.claim: Lesson 3 is titled 'Angels and Predestination' but teaches Risalah, the holy books and the Imamate. Lesson 4 is titled 'Prophethood and the Holy Books' but teaches Al-Qadr, the Day of Judgement, Jannah, Jahannam and Barzakh. Angels are taught in lesson 2, which is titled 'Tawhid and the Nature of Allah'.
findings.truth: Each description matches its own body text, so the titles are the part that is wrong. A straight swap of the two titles does not fix it, because lesson 4 has almost no angel content and lesson 2 carries it. Suggested titles: lesson 2 'Tawhid, the Nature of Allah and Angels'; lesson 3 'Prophethood and the Holy Books'; lesson 4 'Predestination and the Day of Judgement'. Also worth Tom's eye: the second half of lesson 4 (Day of Judgement, Akhirah, Jannah, Jahannam, Barzakh) repeats nearly all of lesson 5.
findings.evidence: raw/L03.txt and raw/L04.txt headings and descriptions against their content_html

findings.claim: 'Max Level 2 if no reference to religion.' in the 12-mark mark scheme of lessons 1, 2, 3 and 4.
findings.truth: Band names 'Level 1' to 'Level 9' are banned house-wide and the validator rejects the whole unit on them. The cap is 6 marks, so the plain statement 'Maximum 6 marks if there is no reference to religion.' says the same thing.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings; the ladder in the same field runs Top 10-12 / Upper-mid 7-9 / Lower-mid 4-6 / Lower 1-3

findings.claim: 'essential for reaching Level 4' (lesson 3) and 'To reach Level 4 (10-12 marks)' (lesson 4).
findings.truth: Same banned band name. Replaced with 'the top band'. The lesson 3 tip also put mark-scheme wording in quotation marks; that quotation is dropped.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings and copyright distancing rule

findings.claim: 6-mark model answer breaks down as Belief 1 (2 marks) + Belief 2 (2 marks) + Source of authority (1 mark).
findings.truth: That sums to 5 on a 6-mark question, and the marking line directly above it says the source is worth 1-2 marks. The source line should read 2 marks.
findings.evidence: recomputation against the same field's own marking line and the spec's 6-mark part

findings.claim: 'Give one Muslim beliefs about Jahannam (hell).' with a key that opens 'Any two of the following, one mark for each:' and closes '[1 mark]'.
findings.truth: The question is worth 1 mark and the key lists two required beliefs, matching the pattern in lessons 1 to 4. The stem should ask for two and the key should award 1 mark for two correct beliefs.
findings.evidence: the same field's own mark total; the 1-mark 'Give/Name' pattern in lessons 1-4

findings.claim: Flashcard answer 'Muhammadrsquos'.
findings.truth: A mangled HTML entity. The answer is Muhammad's.
findings.evidence: raw/L03.txt flashcard 4

findings.claim: Flashcard front begins 'Key Fact _____ is called the “Seal of the Prophets”'.
findings.truth: The words 'Key Fact' are the label of the box the card was scraped from, not part of the sentence.
findings.evidence: raw/L03.txt key-fact block at n7 against flashcard 5

findings.claim: Akhirah is defined as 'The Muslim belief in life after death, beginning at the Day of Judgement.' in the dfn, the glossary and a flashcard.
findings.truth: Akhirah begins at death. The same lesson teaches that Barzakh comes first and its own conclusion says Akhirah 'includes Barzakh (the waiting stage), the Day of Judgement, and the eternal destinations'. The definition as written cuts Barzakh out of Akhirah.
findings.evidence: raw/L05.txt conclusion_html and the Barzakh section against the dfn; spec 3.1.5.1 'Akhirah (life after death)'

findings.claim: 'You need to know five key attributes' under a box headed 'Five Key Qualities of Allah', whose last two entries are 'Fairness and Justice (Al-Adl)' and 'Justice (Adalat in Shi'a Islam)'.
findings.truth: The spec names four: omnipotence, beneficence, mercy, and fairness and justice (Adalat in Shi'a Islam). The fifth entry is the same quality under its Shi'a name, so the count is wrong and a student will hunt for a fifth quality that does not exist.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.1 Key Beliefs: 'The nature of God: omnipotence, beneficence, mercy, fairness and justice/Adalat in Shi'a Islam'

findings.claim: 'They also share the Five Pillars of Islam - the five practices that maintain the Muslim community.' and, in the 12-mark key, 'The Five Pillars are shared.'
findings.truth: The Five Pillars are the Sunni framework. Shi'a Muslims carry out the same five duties but set them inside the Ten Obligatory Acts, which also add khums, jihad, and the commanding of good and forbidding of evil. Telling students the framework is shared is the standard misconception this topic tests.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.2 Worship: 'Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam ... and the additional duties of Shi'a Islam'

findings.claim: Surah 112 quoted as 'He is Allah, the One. Allah is Eternal and Absolute. None is born of Him, He is unborn. There is none like unto Him.'
findings.truth: This stitches three translators together and the third line matches none of them. Abdel Haleem, already the translation used for Surah 9:51 and 18:49 in this unit, reads: 'He is God the One, God the eternal. He begot no one nor was He begotten. No one is comparable to Him.' The later reference to Surah 112 in the same lesson is aligned to the same translation.
findings.evidence: api.quran.com verse 112 (Abdel Haleem id 85, Saheeh International id 20); Wikipedia Al-Ikhlas for Yusuf Ali and Pickthall

findings.claim: Surah 16:90 quoted as 'Indeed Allah commands you towards justice' in lesson 1 body, lesson 1 6-mark key, and lesson 2 body.
findings.truth: No recognised translation reads that way. Saheeh International: 'Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct.' Abdel Haleem: 'God commands justice, doing good, and generosity towards relatives.' Used as the named source on a 6-mark answer, so it must be quotable.
findings.evidence: api.quran.com verse 16:90

findings.claim: Surah 23:102-103 quoted as 'Those whose scales are heavy [with good deeds] will be the successful ones. But those whose scales are light will have lost their souls; in hell they will abide.'
findings.truth: Half Saheeh International, half rewritten. Abdel Haleem: 'those whose good deeds weigh heavy will be successful, but those whose balance is light will have lost their souls for ever and will stay in Hell.' The meaning was right; the wording was not quotable.
findings.evidence: api.quran.com chapter 23 verses 102-103

findings.claim: Three revision tips are broken: 'Can you recall all 5 items listed here?' on a box with no list of five; 'Write down what you recall about shi'a believe in Yawm al-Qiyyamah (the Day.'; 'Recall the specific examples given for belief in Akhirah encourages human.'
findings.truth: Two are truncated mid-sentence and one points at content that is not in the box. Students see these when they tap the box, so they were rewritten as working prompts.
findings.evidence: raw/L05.txt data-revision-tip attributes at n4, n12 and n23

findings.claim: 'Yawm al-Qiyyamah'.
findings.truth: The standard transliteration is Yawm al-Qiyamah, with one y.
findings.evidence: standard transliteration of yawm al-qiyamah

findings.claim: '[12 marks marks]' at the foot of the 12-mark key.
findings.truth: Duplicated word.
findings.evidence: raw/L05.txt practice question 5

findings.claim: 'Understanding both frameworks is essential For the exam .'
findings.truth: A capital F and a floating full stop left behind when a board name was stripped out of the sentence.
findings.evidence: raw/L01.txt n2

findings.claim: Card front 'The ability of humans to make their own choices and decisions...' with the answer 'human freedom'.
findings.truth: The answer word appears in its own question, so the card gives itself away. 'people' carries the same meaning.
findings.evidence: raw/L04.txt flashcard 2; docs/FLASHCARD_RULES.md rule 3

findings.claim: The 6-mark stem reads 'Refer to sacred writings or another source of Muslim belief and teaching in your answer.'
findings.truth: That is the board's own rubric line. Lessons 1 to 4 use the house wording 'Refer to a source of wisdom and authority in your answer.' Left as it stands, because the board wording is what a student will meet in the hall, but flagged under the copyright distancing rule for Tom to settle unit-wide.
findings.evidence: raw/L01-L04 practice question 4 stems against raw/L05.txt

findings.claim: 'According to Islamic teaching, Jannah has seven levels.' plus a knowledge check that marks 'Seven' correct.
findings.truth: This is one attested tradition, drawn from the seven paths of Qur'an 23:17, but other traditions give eight layers from the eight names of paradise. Not wrong enough to edit, and the lesson already teaches the eight gates correctly. Hell having seven levels is well attested (Qur'an 15:44).
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Jannah and Jahannam

findings.claim: All five 12-mark keys open with band descriptors that closely paraphrase the board's own level descriptors ('Well-argued response with reasoned consideration of different points of view, supported by knowledge and religious references').
findings.truth: The banned band names are fixed, but the descriptor wording still sits close to the board's. Rewriting five ladders is a house-style pass, not a fact fix, so it is recorded rather than done here.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md copyright distancing rule

findings.claim: Sunni Muslims are 'around 80-90% of Muslims worldwide' and Shi'a 'around 10-20%'.
findings.truth: Published estimates put Sunni Islam at roughly 87-90% and Shi'a Islam at roughly 10-13%. The Shi'a upper bound of 20% is too high, but the figures appear in three places (dfn, glossary, flashcard) and no exam answer turns on them.
findings.evidence: Pew Research Forum estimates of the global Muslim population

findings.claim: Adam and Hawwa were 'placed in the Garden of Eden'.
findings.truth: Eden is the biblical name. Islamic sources call it the Garden (al-Jannah). Harmless in a GCSE lesson and widely used in UK textbooks, so left alone.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.1 Authority; Qur'an 2:35

summary: No lesson was clean. The unit's exam claims match the spec except lesson 5, which calls the source-of-authority question a 5-mark question when the structure is 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12; four 12-mark keys and two exam tips carry the banned 'Level' band names that would fail the validator. Three Qur'an quotations (112, 16:90, 23:102-103) were stitched paraphrases rather than any recognised translation, the Five Pillars were described as shared with Shi'a Islam, lesson 2 promises five qualities of Allah where the spec names four, and lesson 5 defines Akhirah as starting at the Day of Judgement while teaching that Barzakh comes first. Lesson 3 and lesson 4 also carry titles that belong to other lessons; that one needs Tom, because title is not an editable field here.
